Creating a batch script to automate skin processing for Fedmonster. It will:
1. Process the BMP for all armor types (larmor, marmor, harmor, lfemale, mfemale)
2. Create a volume with all processed skins
3. Copy the volume to the target directory


---

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="write">

<details><summary>Tool use: **write** • Edit file: C:\Users\Joe\Desktop\Extracted RPG Skins\SkinTools\MakeFedmonsterSkin.bat</summary>

**Chunk 1**
Lines added: 125, lines removed: 1

```diff
@@ -1,1 +1,125 @@
- 
+ @echo off
+ REM ============================================
+ REM Starsiege Tribes 1 Skin Automation Script
+ REM For Fedmonster skin creation
+ REM ============================================
+ 
+ setlocal enabledelayedexpansion
+ 
+ REM Set paths
+ set "SKINTOOLS_DIR=%~dp0"
+ set "TARGET_DIR=C:\Dynamix\Tribes\RPG\Skins"
+ set "PALETTE=pal3"
+ set "PREFIX=fedmonster"
+ set "VOLUME_NAME=%PREFIX%Skins.vol"
+ 
+ REM Check if input file was provided
+ if "%~1"=="" (
+     echo.
+     echo Usage: MakeFedmonsterSkin.bat [input.bmp]
+     echo   Or drag and drop a BMP file onto this script
+     echo.
+     echo If no file is provided, will look for BMP files in current directory.
+     echo.
+     pause
+     exit /b 1
+ )
+ 
+ set "INPUT_FILE=%~1"
+ 
+ REM Check if input file exists
+ if not exist "%INPUT_FILE%" (
+     echo ERROR: Input file not found: %INPUT_FILE%
+     pause
+     exit /b 1
+ )
+ 
+ echo.
+ echo ============================================
+ echo Processing Fedmonster Skin
+ echo ============================================
+ echo Input file: %INPUT_FILE%
+ echo Palette: %PALETTE%
+ echo Prefix: %PREFIX%
+ echo.
+ 
+ REM Change to SkinTools directory
+ cd /d "%SKINTOOLS_DIR%"
+ 
+ REM Define armor types
+ set "ARMOR_TYPES=larmor marmor harmor lfemale mfemale"
+ 
+ REM Remove old volume if it exists
+ if exist "%VOLUME_NAME%" (
+     echo Removing old volume: %VOLUME_NAME%
+     del "%VOLUME_NAME%"
+ )
+ 
+ REM Process each armor type
+ echo Processing skins...
+ for %%A in (%ARMOR_TYPES%) do (
+     set "OUTPUT_FILE=%PREFIX%.%%A.bmp"
+     echo.
+     echo Processing: %%A
+     echo   Input:  %INPUT_FILE%
+     echo   Output: !OUTPUT_FILE!
+     
+     REM Run makeskin
+     "%SKINTOOLS_DIR%MakeSkin.exe" %PALETTE% "%INPUT_FILE%" "!OUTPUT_FILE!"
+     
+     if errorlevel 1 (
+         echo ERROR: Failed to process %%A
+         pause
+         exit /b 1
+     )
+     
+     REM Add to volume
+     echo Adding to volume...
+     "%SKINTOOLS_DIR%VT.EXE" -sp "%VOLUME_NAME%" "!OUTPUT_FILE!"
+     
+     if errorlevel 1 (
+         echo ERROR: Failed to add %%A to volume
+         pause
+         exit /b 1
+     )
+ )
+ 
+ REM Verify volume contents
+ echo.
+ echo ============================================
+ echo Verifying volume contents...
+ echo ============================================
+ "%SKINTOOLS_DIR%VT.EXE" "%VOLUME_NAME%"
+ 
+ REM Check if target directory exists
+ if not exist "%TARGET_DIR%" (
+     echo.
+     echo WARNING: Target directory does not exist: %TARGET_DIR%
+     echo Creating directory...
+     mkdir "%TARGET_DIR%"
+ )
+ 
+ REM Copy volume to target directory
+ echo.
+ echo ============================================
+ echo Copying volume to target directory...
+ echo ============================================
+ copy "%VOLUME_NAME%" "%TARGET_DIR%\" &gt;nul
+ 
+ if errorlevel 1 (
+     echo ERROR: Failed to copy volume to target directory
+     pause
+     exit /b 1
+ )
+ 
+ echo.
+ echo ============================================
+ echo SUCCESS!
+ echo ============================================
+ echo Volume created: %VOLUME_NAME%
+ echo Volume copied to: %TARGET_DIR%
+ echo.
+ echo Your Fedmonster skin is ready!
+ echo.
+ pause
+ 
```

</details>

</tool-use>

Created `MakeFedmonsterSkin.bat` to automate the process. It:

1. **Processes your BMP file** for all 5 armor types (larmor, marmor, harmor, lfemale, mfemale)
2. **Creates a volume** (`fedmonsterSkins.vol`) containing all processed skins
3. **Copies the volume** to `C:\Dynamix\Tribes\RPG\Skins`

## How to use:

**Option 1: Drag and drop**
- Drag your 8-bit indexed BMP file onto `MakeFedmonsterSkin.bat`

**Option 2: Command line**
- Run: `MakeFedmonsterSkin.bat "path\to\your\skin.bmp"`

**Important notes:**
- Your input BMP must be 8-bit indexed color using the `pal3` palette (included in the palettes folder)
- The script uses `pal3` (recommended per the readme)
- All processed skins will be named: `fedmonster.larmor.bmp`, `fedmonster.marmor.bmp`, etc.
- The final volume will be automatically copied to your Tribes skins directory

The script will show progress and verify the volume contents before copying it to the target directory.

If you want to customize the prefix (currently "fedmonster") or change any settings, I can update the script.

+     
+     if errorlevel 1 (
+         echo WARNING: Palette conversion failed. Using original file.
+         echo Make sure your input BMP is already in 8-bit indexed color using pal3.
+         set "USE_CONVERTED=0"
+     ) else (
+         if exist "%CONVERTED_FILE%" (
+             echo Successfully converted to pal3 palette!
+             set "USE_CONVERTED=1"
+             set "INPUT_FILE=%CONVERTED_FILE%"
+         ) else (
+             echo WARNING: Converted file not found. Using original file.
+             set "USE_CONVERTED=0"
+         )
+     )
+     echo.
+ ) else (
+     echo ============================================
+     echo ImageMagick not found - skipping palette conversion
+     echo ============================================
+     echo NOTE: Your input BMP must already be in 8-bit indexed color using pal3 palette.

Updated the script to automatically convert images to the `pal3PS.act` palette. It:

1. **Checks for ImageMagick** — if installed, uses it to convert the image
2. **Converts the palette** — remaps colors to `pal3PS.act` using Floyd-Steinberg dithering
3. **Uses the converted file** — processes the palette-converted version
4. **Cleans up** — removes the temporary converted file after processing

**How it works:**
- If ImageMagick is installed: automatically converts your BMP to use the `pal3PS.act` palette before processing
- If ImageMagick is not installed: shows a warning and continues (assumes your BMP is already in the correct format)

**To use ImageMagick (optional but recommended):**
1. Download from: https://imagemagick.org/script/download.php
2. Install it (make sure to check "Add to PATH" during installation)
3. The script will automatically detect and use it

You can drag any BMP onto the script, and it will convert it to the correct palette and process it for all armor types. If ImageMagick isn't installed, the script still works, but you'll need to manually convert your BMP to 8-bit indexed color using the `pal3` palette first.

---


For your system (Windows 10 64-bit), use:

**Recommended: `ImageMagick-7.1.2-10-Q16-x64-dll.exe`**
- 64-bit Windows
- Dynamic linking (smaller install)
- Q16 (16-bit depth; fine for 8-bit palette conversion)
- Standard installer

**Alternative: `ImageMagick-7.1.2-10-portable-Q16-x64.7z`**
- Portable (no install, no registry)
- Extract and run
- Requires 7-Zip

**Why not the others:**
- Q8: Works, but Q16 is more common and versatile
- Static: Larger download
- HDRI: Not needed for palette conversion
- ARM64/x86: Wrong architecture

**Installation tip:** During setup, check "Add application directory to your system path" so the batch script can find `magick`.

The script will detect ImageMagick after installation and use it for palette conversion.

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="write">

<details><summary>Tool use: **write** • Edit file: C:\Users\Joe\Desktop\Extracted RPG Skins\SkinTools\ConvertToPBMP.bat</summary>

Lines added: 122, lines removed: 1

```diff
@@ -1,1 +1,122 @@
- 
+ @echo off
+ REM ============================================
+ REM Convert BMP to PBMP Format
+ REM Uses MakeSkin.exe to convert 8-bit BMP files to PBMP (Tribes format)
+ REM ============================================
+ 
+ setlocal enabledelayedexpansion
+ 
+ REM Set paths
+ set "SKINTOOLS_DIR=%~dp0"
+ set "PALETTE=pal3"
+ 
+ REM Check if input file was provided
+ if "%~1"=="" (
+     echo.
+     echo Usage: ConvertToPBMP.bat [input.bmp] [output.bmp]
+     echo   Or drag and drop a BMP file onto this script
+     echo.
+     echo This script converts 8-bit BMP files to PBMP format (Tribes-optimized)
+     echo using MakeSkin.exe with the pal3 palette.
+     echo.
+     echo If only one file is provided, output will be: [filename]_pbmp.bmp
+     echo.
+     pause
+     exit /b 1
+ )
+ 
+ set "INPUT_FILE=%~1"
+ set "OUTPUT_FILE=%~2"
+ 
+ REM Check if input file exists
+ if not exist "%INPUT_FILE%" (
+     echo ERROR: Input file not found: %INPUT_FILE%
+     pause
+     exit /b 1
+ )
+ 
+ REM If output file not specified, create one based on input filename
+ if "!OUTPUT_FILE!"=="" (
+     set "INPUT_BASE=%~n1"
+     set "INPUT_DIR=%~dp1"
+     set "OUTPUT_FILE=%INPUT_DIR%%INPUT_BASE%_pbmp.bmp"
+ )
+ 
+ echo.
+ echo ============================================
+ echo Converting BMP to PBMP Format
+ echo ============================================
+ echo Input file:  %INPUT_FILE%
+ echo Output file: %OUTPUT_FILE%
+ echo Palette:     %PALETTE%
+ echo.
+ echo Note: MakeSkin.exe converts BMP to PBMP format (Tribes-optimized)
+ echo       Output files use .bmp extension but are in PBMP format internally
+ echo.
+ 
+ REM Change to SkinTools directory
+ cd /d "%SKINTOOLS_DIR%"
+ 
+ REM Check if MakeSkin.exe exists
+ if not exist "%SKINTOOLS_DIR%MakeSkin.exe" (
+     echo ERROR: MakeSkin.exe not found in %SKINTOOLS_DIR%
+     echo Please ensure MakeSkin.exe is in the same directory as this script.
+     pause
+     exit /b 1
+ )
+ 
+ REM Check if palette file exists
+ set "PALETTE_PAL=%SKINTOOLS_DIR%palettes\%PALETTE%.pal"
+ set "PALETTE_ACT=%SKINTOOLS_DIR%palettes\%PALETTE%PS.act"
+ if not exist "%PALETTE_PAL%" (
+     if not exist "%PALETTE_ACT%" (
+         echo WARNING: Palette file not found in palettes folder.
+         echo MakeSkin will look for %PALETTE%.pal in current directory.
+     )
+ )
+ 
+ REM Run MakeSkin.exe to convert to PBMP
+ echo Converting to PBMP format...
+ echo Command: MakeSkin.exe %PALETTE% "%INPUT_FILE%" "%OUTPUT_FILE%"
+ echo.
+ 
+ "%SKINTOOLS_DIR%MakeSkin.exe" %PALETTE% "%INPUT_FILE%" "%OUTPUT_FILE%"
+ 
+ if errorlevel 1 (
+     echo.
+     echo ERROR: MakeSkin.exe conversion failed!
+     echo.
+     echo Make sure:
+     echo   - Input file is an 8-bit indexed BMP file
+     echo   - Input file is 256x256 pixels (or will be resized)
+     echo   - Palette file (%PALETTE%.pal) is available
+     echo.
+     pause
+     exit /b 1
+ )
+ 
+ REM Verify output file was created
+ if not exist "%OUTPUT_FILE%" (
+     echo.
+     echo ERROR: Output file was not created: %OUTPUT_FILE%
+     pause
+     exit /b 1
+ )
+ 
+ REM Get file size for verification
+ for %%F in ("%OUTPUT_FILE%") do set "OUTPUT_SIZE=%%~zF"
+ 
+ echo.
+ echo ============================================
+ echo SUCCESS!
+ echo ============================================
+ echo File converted to PBMP format successfully!
+ echo.
+ echo Output file: %OUTPUT_FILE%
+ echo File size:   %OUTPUT_SIZE% bytes
+ echo.
+ echo Note: PBMP files use .bmp extension but contain PBMP format internally.
+ echo       This is the Tribes-optimized bitmap format.
+ echo.
+ pause
+ 
```

Created `ConvertToPBMP.bat` — a standalone batch file that converts BMP files to PBMP format.

**Features:**
- **Drag and drop**: Drag a BMP file onto the script
- **Command line**: `ConvertToPBMP.bat input.bmp output.bmp`
- **Auto-naming**: If no output is specified, creates `[filename]_pbmp.bmp`
- **Uses MakeSkin.exe** with the pal3 palette to convert to PBMP format
- **Verification**: Checks that the output file was created and shows file size

**Usage examples:**
1. **Drag and drop**: Drag `skin.bmp` onto `ConvertToPBMP.bat` → creates `skin_pbmp.bmp`
2. **With output name**: `ConvertToPBMP.bat skin.bmp output.bmp` → creates `output.bmp` in PBMP format
3. **Command line**: Run from command prompt with file paths

**Requirements:**
- Input file must be an 8-bit indexed BMP
- MakeSkin.exe must be in the same folder
- Palette files should be in the `palettes` folder

The script converts a single BMP file to PBMP format, separate from the full skin processing pipeline.

This is a blender plungin that converts pictures to the proper 8 bit DBMP 



 the logic is pretty simple.  Treat the palette file as an array of pixels from 0-255.  In your .png you go pixel by pixel in the image, find the color (3 rgb bytes) that matches the color in the palette, and replace that with the index of that color in the palette.  The result looks gray scale because you are taking the 3 bytes of color and replacing it with 1 byte

@@ -1,1 +1,109 @@
- 
+ #!/usr/bin/env python3
+ """
+ Apply ACT palette to image - converts RGB colors to palette indices
+ This implements the same logic as the Blender plugin: find closest color in palette
+ and replace RGB with palette index (0-255)
+ """
+ 
+ import sys
+ import struct
+ from PIL import Image
+ import numpy as np
+ 
+ def read_act_palette(act_file):
+     """Read ACT palette file and return array of RGB colors"""
+     palette = []
+     with open(act_file, 'rb') as f:
+         for i in range(256):
+             rgb = f.read(3)
+             if len(rgb) &lt; 3:
+                 break
+             palette.append((rgb[0], rgb[1], rgb[2]))
+     return palette
+ 
+ def find_closest_color(rgb, palette):
+     """Find the index of the closest color in the palette using Euclidean distance"""
+     r, g, b = rgb
+     min_dist = float('inf')
+     best_index = 0
+     
+     for i, (pr, pg, pb) in enumerate(palette):
+         # Euclidean distance in RGB space
+         dist = ((r - pr) ** 2 + (g - pg) ** 2 + (b - pb) ** 2) ** 0.5
+         if dist &lt; min_dist:
+             min_dist = dist
+             best_index = i
+             if dist == 0:  # Exact match
+                 break
+     
+     return best_index
+ 
+ def apply_palette(input_file, output_file, palette_file):
+     """Apply palette to image - convert RGB to palette indices"""
+     print(f"Reading palette from: {palette_file}")
+     palette = read_act_palette(palette_file)
+     print(f"Loaded {len(palette)} colors from palette")
+     
+     print(f"Loading image: {input_file}")
+     img = Image.open(input_file)
+     
+     # Convert to RGB if needed
+     if img.mode != 'RGB':
+         img = img.convert('RGB')
+     
+     # Resize to 256x256 if needed
+     if img.size != (256, 256):
+         print(f"Resizing from {img.size} to 256x256")
+         img = img.resize((256, 256), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
+     
+     print("Applying palette (finding closest color for each pixel)...")
+     # Convert to numpy array for faster processing
+     pixels = np.array(img)
+     height, width = pixels.shape[:2]
+     
+     # Create output array (grayscale - palette indices)
+     output = np.zeros((height, width), dtype=np.uint8)
+     
+     # Process each pixel
+     for y in range(height):
+         for x in range(width):
+             r, g, b = pixels[y, x]
+             index = find_closest_color((r, g, b), palette)
+             output[y, x] = index
+     
+     print(f"Saving indexed image: {output_file}")
+     # Create indexed image with the palette
+     indexed_img = Image.fromarray(output, mode='P')
+     
+     # Set the palette
+     palette_data = []
+     for r, g, b in palette:
+         palette_data.extend([r, g, b])
+     # Pad to 256 colors (768 bytes)
+     while len(palette_data) &lt; 768:
+         palette_data.append(0)
+     
+     indexed_img.putpalette(palette_data)
+     
+     # Save as 8-bit BMP
+     indexed_img.save(output_file, 'BMP')
+     print(f"Successfully created 8-bit indexed BMP: {output_file}")
+ 
+ if __name__ == '__main__':
+     if len(sys.argv) != 4:
+         print("Usage: ApplyPalette.py &lt;input.png&gt; &lt;output.bmp&gt; &lt;palette.act&gt;")
+         print("  Converts image to 8-bit indexed BMP using the specified ACT palette")
+         sys.exit(1)
+     
+     input_file = sys.argv[1]
+     output_file = sys.argv[2]
+     palette_file = sys.argv[3]
+     
+     try:
+         apply_palette(input_file, output_file, palette_file)
+     except Exception as e:
+         print(f"Error: {e}")
+         import traceback
+         traceback.print_exc()
+         sys.exit(1)
+

Created a Python script that implements the same palette remapping logic as your Blender plugin:

**What the Python script does:**
1. Reads the ACT palette file as an array of 256 RGB colors (0-255)
2. Goes pixel-by-pixel through the image
3. Finds the closest matching color in the palette using Euclidean distance
4. Replaces the RGB value with the palette index (0-255)
5. Creates an 8-bit indexed BMP with the palette applied

**Integration:**
- The batch script now uses this Python script as the preferred method
- Falls back to nconvert if Python isn't available
- Falls back to ImageMagick if neither is available

**Requirements:**
- Python 3 with PIL/Pillow installed: `pip install Pillow numpy`

The script will automatically:
- Resize images to 256x256
- Apply the pal3 palette using pixel-by-pixel remapping
- Create a proper 8-bit indexed BMP that MakeSkin.exe can process

This should produce better results than ImageMagick or nconvert because it matches the Blender plugin logic. Try running the script again; it should use the Python method if Python is installed.

**What's set up:**

- Pillow and numpy installed
- `ApplyPalette.py` script created and working
- Batch script updated to use Python as the preferred method

**How it works:**
1. The batch script detects Python
2. Runs `ApplyPalette.py` which does pixel-by-pixel palette remapping (same logic as your Blender plugin)
3. Creates an 8-bit indexed BMP with the pal3 palette applied
4. MakeSkin.exe converts it to PBMP format

**To use it:**
Drag and drop a BMP or PNG file onto `MakeFedmonsterSkin.bat`. It will:
- Use Python for accurate palette conversion (pixel-by-pixel matching)
- Fall back to nconvert if Python isn't available
- Fall back to ImageMagick if neither is available

The Python method should give better results because it matches the Blender plugin's logic: finding the closest color in the palette for each pixel and replacing RGB with the palette index (0-255).

Fixed the delayed expansion issue. Since the script uses `setlocal enabledelayedexpansion`, variables set inside blocks must be read with `!variable!` instead of `%variable%`.

**What I fixed:**
- Changed `%USE_CONVERTED%` to `!USE_CONVERTED!` in all conditional checks
- This ensures the variable is read correctly when set inside the if blocks

The script should work now. Try running it again; it should no longer close immediately. The syntax error was caused by mixing normal expansion (`%variable%`) with delayed expansion (`!variable!`) in a delayed expansion context.

@@ -1,1 +1,132 @@
- 
+ #!/usr/bin/env python3
+ """
+ Convert image to 8-bit indexed BMP using ACT palette
+ Uses pixel-by-pixel remapping: find closest color in palette, replace RGB with index (0-255)
+ """
+ 
+ import sys
+ import os
+ from PIL import Image
+ import numpy as np
+ 
+ def read_act_palette(act_file):
+     """Read ACT palette file - 256 RGB colors (3 bytes each = 768 bytes)"""
+     palette = []
+     with open(act_file, 'rb') as f:
+         for i in range(256):
+             rgb = f.read(3)
+             if len(rgb) &lt; 3:
+                 # Pad with black if file is shorter
+                 rgb = rgb + b'\x00' * (3 - len(rgb))
+             palette.append((rgb[0], rgb[1], rgb[2]))
+     return palette
+ 
+ def find_closest_color(rgb, palette):
+     """Find the index of the closest color in the palette using Euclidean distance"""
+     r, g, b = rgb
+     min_dist = float('inf')
+     best_index = 0
+     
+     for i, (pr, pg, pb) in enumerate(palette):
+         # Euclidean distance in RGB space
+         dist = ((r - pr) ** 2 + (g - pg) ** 2 + (b - pb) ** 2) ** 0.5
+         if dist &lt; min_dist:
+             min_dist = dist
+             best_index = i
+             if dist == 0:  # Exact match
+                 break
+     
+     return best_index
+ 
+ def convert_image(input_file, output_file, palette_file):
+     """Convert image to 8-bit indexed BMP using ACT palette"""
+     print(f"Reading palette from: {palette_file}")
+     palette = read_act_palette(palette_file)
+     print(f"Loaded {len(palette)} colors from palette")
+     
+     print(f"Loading image: {input_file}")
+     img = Image.open(input_file)
+     
+     # Convert to RGB if needed
+     if img.mode != 'RGB':
+         img = img.convert('RGB')
+     
+     # Resize to 256x256 if needed
+     if img.size != (256, 256):
+         print(f"Resizing from {img.size} to 256x256")
+         img = img.resize((256, 256), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
+     
+     print("Applying palette (pixel-by-pixel remapping)...")
+     print("  Finding closest palette color for each pixel...")
+     print("  Replacing RGB values with palette indices (0-255)...")
+     
+     # Convert to numpy array for faster processing
+     pixels = np.array(img)
+     height, width = pixels.shape[:2]
+     
+     # Create output array (grayscale - palette indices)
+     output = np.zeros((height, width), dtype=np.uint8)
+     
+     # Process each pixel
+     total_pixels = height * width
+     processed = 0
+     for y in range(height):
+         for x in range(width):
+             r, g, b = pixels[y, x]
+             index = find_closest_color((r, g, b), palette)
+             output[y, x] = index
+             processed += 1
+             if processed % 10000 == 0:
+                 print(f"  Processed {processed}/{total_pixels} pixels...")
+     
+     print(f"  Completed {total_pixels} pixels")
+     
+     print(f"Creating indexed image with palette...")
+     # Create indexed image with the palette
+     indexed_img = Image.fromarray(output, mode='P')
+     
+     # Set the palette (PIL expects 768 bytes: 256 colors * 3 bytes RGB)
+     palette_data = []
+     for r, g, b in palette:
+         palette_data.extend([r, g, b])
+     # Pad to exactly 768 bytes if needed
+     while len(palette_data) &lt; 768:
+         palette_data.append(0)
+     palette_data = palette_data[:768]  # Ensure exactly 768 bytes
+     
+     indexed_img.putpalette(palette_data)
+     
+     print(f"Saving 8-bit indexed BMP: {output_file}")
+     # Save as 8-bit BMP
+     indexed_img.save(output_file, 'BMP')
+     print(f"Successfully created 8-bit indexed BMP: {output_file}")
+     print(f"  File size: {os.path.getsize(output_file)} bytes")
+ 
+ if __name__ == '__main__':
+     if len(sys.argv) != 4:
+         print("Usage: ConvertSkin.py &lt;input.png|bmp&gt; &lt;output.bmp&gt; &lt;palette.act&gt;")
+         print("  Converts image to 8-bit indexed BMP using the specified ACT palette")
+         print("  Logic: Pixel-by-pixel remapping - finds closest color in palette,")
+         print("         replaces RGB (3 bytes) with palette index (1 byte, 0-255)")
+         sys.exit(1)
+     
+     input_file = sys.argv[1]
+     output_file = sys.argv[2]
+     palette_file = sys.argv[3]
+     
+     if not os.path.exists(input_file):
+         print(f"Error: Input file not found: {input_file}")
+         sys.exit(1)
+     
+     if not os.path.exists(palette_file):
+         print(f"Error: Palette file not found: {palette_file}")
+         sys.exit(1)
+     
+     try:
+         convert_image(input_file, output_file, palette_file)
+     except Exception as e:
+         print(f"Error: {e}")
+         import traceback
+         traceback.print_exc()
+         sys.exit(1)
+

@@ -1,1 +1,140 @@

+ #!/usr/bin/env python3
+ """
+ Convert image to 8-bit indexed BMP using ACT palette for loading screens
+ Uses pixel-by-pixel remapping: find closest color in palette, replace RGB with index (0-255)
+ Outputs at 640x480 resolution
+ """
+ 
+ import sys
+ import os
+ from PIL import Image
+ import numpy as np
+ 
+ def read_act_palette(act_file):
+     """Read ACT palette file - 256 RGB colors (3 bytes each = 768 bytes)"""
+     palette = []
+     with open(act_file, 'rb') as f:
+         for i in range(256):
+             rgb = f.read(3)
+             if len(rgb) &lt; 3:
+                 # Pad with black if file is shorter
+                 rgb = rgb + b'\x00' * (3 - len(rgb))
+             palette.append((rgb[0], rgb[1], rgb[2]))
+     return palette
+ 
+ def find_closest_color(rgb, palette):
+     """Find the index of the closest color in the palette using Euclidean distance"""
+     r, g, b = int(rgb[0]), int(rgb[1]), int(rgb[2])
+     min_dist = float('inf')
+     best_index = 0
+     
+     for i, (pr, pg, pb) in enumerate(palette):
+         # Euclidean distance in RGB space (use int to avoid overflow warnings)
+         dr = int(r) - int(pr)
+         dg = int(g) - int(pg)
+         db = int(b) - int(pb)
+         dist = (dr * dr + dg * dg + db * db) ** 0.5
+         if dist &lt; min_dist:
+             min_dist = dist
+             best_index = i
+             if dist == 0:  # Exact match
+                 break
+     
+     return best_index
+ 
+ def convert_image(input_file, output_file, palette_file, width=640, height=480):
+     """Convert image to 8-bit indexed BMP using ACT palette"""
+     print(f"Reading palette from: {palette_file}")
+     palette = read_act_palette(palette_file)
+     print(f"Loaded {len(palette)} colors from palette")
+     
+     print(f"Loading image: {input_file}")
+     img = Image.open(input_file)
+     
+     # Convert to RGB if needed
+     if img.mode != 'RGB':
+         img = img.convert('RGB')
+     
+     # Resize to specified dimensions if needed
+     if img.size != (width, height):
+         print(f"Resizing from {img.size} to {width}x{height}")
+         img = img.resize((width, height), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
+     
+     print(f"Applying palette (pixel-by-pixel remapping) to {width}x{height} image...")
+     print("  Finding closest palette color for each pixel...")
+     print("  Replacing RGB values with palette indices (0-255)...")
+     
+     # Convert to numpy array for faster processing
+     pixels = np.array(img)
+     img_height, img_width = pixels.shape[:2]
+     
+     # Create output array (grayscale - palette indices)
+     output = np.zeros((img_height, img_width), dtype=np.uint8)
+     
+     # Process each pixel
+     total_pixels = img_height * img_width
+     processed = 0
+     for y in range(img_height):
+         for x in range(img_width):
+             r, g, b = pixels[y, x]
+             index = find_closest_color((r, g, b), palette)
+             output[y, x] = index
+             processed += 1
+             if processed % 10000 == 0:
+                 print(f"  Processed {processed}/{total_pixels} pixels...")
+     
+     print(f"  Completed {total_pixels} pixels")
+     
+     print(f"Creating indexed image with palette...")
+     # Create indexed image with the palette
+     indexed_img = Image.fromarray(output, mode='P')
+     
+     # Set the palette (PIL expects 768 bytes: 256 colors * 3 bytes RGB)
+     palette_data = []
+     for r, g, b in palette:
+         palette_data.extend([r, g, b])
+     # Pad to exactly 768 bytes if needed
+     while len(palette_data) &lt; 768:
+         palette_data.append(0)
+     palette_data = palette_data[:768]  # Ensure exactly 768 bytes
+     
+     indexed_img.putpalette(palette_data)
+     
+     print(f"Saving 8-bit indexed BMP: {output_file}")
+     # Save as 8-bit BMP
+     indexed_img.save(output_file, 'BMP')
+     print(f"Successfully created 8-bit indexed BMP: {output_file}")
+     print(f"  Resolution: {width}x{height}")
+     print(f"  File size: {os.path.getsize(output_file)} bytes")
+ 
+ if __name__ == '__main__':
+     if len(sys.argv) &lt; 4:
+         print("Usage: ConvertLoadingScreen.py &lt;input.png|bmp&gt; &lt;output.bmp&gt; &lt;palette.act&gt; [width] [height]")
+         print("  Converts image to 8-bit indexed BMP using the specified ACT palette")
+         print("  Default resolution: 640x480")
+         print("  Logic: Pixel-by-pixel remapping - finds closest color in palette,")
+         print("         replaces RGB (3 bytes) with palette index (1 byte, 0-255)")
+         sys.exit(1)
+     
+     input_file = sys.argv[1]
+     output_file = sys.argv[2]
+     palette_file = sys.argv[3]
+     width = int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) &gt; 4 else 640
+     height = int(sys.argv[5]) if len(sys.argv) &gt; 5 else 480
+     
+     if not os.path.exists(input_file):
+         print(f"Error: Input file not found: {input_file}")
+         sys.exit(1)
+     
+     if not os.path.exists(palette_file):
+         print(f"Error: Palette file not found: {palette_file}")
+         sys.exit(1)
+     
+     try:
+         convert_image(input_file, output_file, palette_file, width, height)
+     except Exception as e:
+         print(f"Error: {e}")
+         import traceback
+         traceback.print_exc()
+         sys.exit(1)
+
